Spec edit landed: commit `80d5e11` (2026-05-11 21:15 PDT) on the jmap-chat-spec repo `main` branch.

## What landed vs. what was originally planned

The original bead description proposed removing 8 cap-advertising fields. The actual edit removed 5:

- Dropped: `maxGroupMembers`, `maxSpaceMembers`, `maxRolesPerSpace`, `maxChannelsPerSpace`, `maxCategoriesPerSpace`
- Kept: `maxBodyBytes`, `maxAttachmentBytes`, `maxAttachmentsPerMessage`

Rationale for the narrower scope (per the commit message): the 5 dropped fields had no analog in any other JMAP spec; the 3 kept fields have direct analogs in `urn:ietf:params:jmap:mail` (RFC 8621 — `maxSizeAttachmentsPerEmail` etc.), where the per-message-size caps live on the capability and are part of the established JMAP pattern. Removing those would deviate from RFC 8621 precedent.

The kept 3 caps continue to be advertised on the capability. The 5 dropped caps are now implementation-defined and enforced via standard `overQuota` SetError (RFC 8620 §5.3) at exceed time, with account-level visibility recommended via JMAP Quotas (RFC 9425) as a SHOULD.

## Spec edits performed

All the concrete edits listed in the bead description were performed within the narrowed scope:

- Lines 156–186: removed the 5 dropped field definitions; kept the 3 kept fields and `supportedBodyTypes`/`supportsThreads`.
- Line 188: Quota integration note rewritten; now cites RFC 9425 and clarifies per-aggregate `overQuota` mechanism.
- Lines 886, 903 (Group/set membership caps): replaced with `overQuota` language.
- Lines 1095, 1105, 1114, 1123 (Space/set addRoles/addMembers/addChannels/addCategories caps): replaced with `overQuota` language.
- Line 1447 (DoS section): retained `maxBodyBytes`/`maxAttachmentBytes`/`maxAttachmentsPerMessage` references (those caps still exist); added implementation-defined per-aggregate language with `overQuota`.
- Bibliography: replaced `JMAP-QUOTAS` draft reference with `RFC9425`.

Also fixed a pre-existing bug: the Quota integration paragraph used `datatypes` instead of the correct `types` field name per RFC 9425 §4.1.

## Workspace catch-up

The workspace-side cleanup (chat-client `ChatCapability` struct still carries the 5 dropped fields; chat-server has one stale doc comment) is tracked by JMAP-v3ff.

JMAP-g7wu.2.4.8 (Space/set count-limit enforcement implementation) remains actionable; the `ChatLimits` + `overQuota` shape in its design notes matches the new spec mandate.
description:
Captured from JMAP-g7wu.2.4.8 design discussion (2026-05-11, Mark).

The current draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §The urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat Capability (lines 154-186) defines 8 `max*` fields under `accountCapabilities["urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat"]` and mandates server enforcement of those caps throughout the document. **The spec should not have fixed caps at all.**

## Rationale

  1. **Implementations cannot agree on numbers.** A single-user homeserver wants tight defaults; a multi-tenant SaaS wants tier-dependent caps; a federation-mode relay has different needs again. Fixed numeric defaults in the spec force every implementer to either accept inappropriate numbers or deviate (silently breaking interop assumptions).
  
  2. **Deployment modes are too diverse.** The spec already documents two deployment topologies (mailbox-per-user, relay); cap needs differ by an order of magnitude or more between them. Per-account caps in account capabilities can't sensibly serve both.
  
  3. **JMAP Quotas extension already exists** (`urn:ietf:params:jmap:quotas`, currently informally referenced at line 188). The Quota data type exposes `hardLimit` and `usage` dynamically. This is the right cross-protocol mechanism for "client wants to know cap before it tries something" — strictly better than static capability fields because it carries dynamic usage too.
  
  4. **Premature standardization.** Nobody has years of operational experience with JMAP chat at scale; locking numbers into the spec now ossifies guesses.
  
  5. **Spec stability.** Removing the cap fields simplifies the spec. They can be added back in a future revision if real-world interop pain demands it.

## Concrete spec edits

  - **Lines 156-186** (account-capability `max*` fields): remove all 8 cap field definitions: `maxBodyBytes`, `maxAttachmentBytes`, `maxAttachmentsPerMessage`, `maxGroupMembers`, `maxSpaceMembers`, `maxRolesPerSpace`, `maxChannelsPerSpace`, `maxCategoriesPerSpace`. Keep `supportedBodyTypes` and `supportsThreads` — those are capability negotiation, not caps.
  
  - **Line 188** (Quota integration note): promote from "Note: also..." to the primary mechanism for exposing caps to clients. Drop the phrase "beyond the static capability limits defined above" — there are no static capability limits to be "beyond".
  
  - **Lines 886, 903** (Group/set `maxGroupMembers` enforcement): drop "Total membership ... MUST NOT exceed `maxGroupMembers`" language. Replace with implementation-defined-limits language and a reference to JMAP Quota.
  
  - **Lines 1095, 1105, 1114, 1123** (Space/set add* caps): drop "Total MUST NOT exceed maxXxxx" language for addRoles / addMembers / addChannels / addCategories. Same replacement.
  
  - **Line 1447** (`maxBodyBytes` enforcement at message parse): drop the `maxBodyBytes` reference. The general "validate UTF-8 for plaintext body types" stays.
  
  - **Line 1460** (enforcement summary): rewrite without naming caps. Keep the parse-time-vs-creation-time enforcement cadence as a general rule ("servers MUST enforce their configured caps at parse / creation / update time") without enumerating which caps.
  
  - **§The urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat Capability** (header at line 144): possibly reorganize / shorten since the section's main payload is now just `supportedBodyTypes` + `supportsThreads`.

## What this does NOT change

  - Servers are still free (and expected) to enforce their own configured caps. The spec just doesn't define what those caps are or how they're communicated to clients beyond JMAP Quota.
  - JMAP Quota integration becomes the canonical "client-visible caps" mechanism. Spec language SHOULD encourage servers to implement Quota, but cannot MUST it without a separate dependency.
  - Workspace implementation in JMAP-g7wu.2.4.8 continues as-is: `ChatBackend::limits()` method returning conservative defaults, backend enforces at creation/update time. Just no spec contract for the specific values.

## Acceptance

  - Next draft-atwood-jmap-chat revision (likely -01) has cap fields fully removed from §Account Capability.
  - All "MUST NOT exceed maxXxxx" language removed throughout the document.
  - Quota integration language strengthened to be the primary mechanism for cap visibility.
  - Workspace JMAP-g7wu.2.4.8 implementation no longer claims spec-mandated enforcement of named caps; it claims implementation-defined per-Space content limits with a backend-trait method exposing them.
  - Federation draft (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation) audited for any cap references that need parallel removal (likely none, but verify).

## Scope

Spec-author work only. No workspace code changes — the implementation continues against the revised spec.

## Cross-references

  - JMAP-g7wu.2.4.8 — workspace implementation bead; its notes updated 2026-05-11 to reflect the new spec posture
  - JMAP-4ir7 — sibling spec-author bead (group chat admin model)
  - JMAP-g7wu.2.4.11 — sibling spec-author work (Space.ownerId field addition)
